facts.text: Natrona Heights began as a pioneer farming community in the early 1800s before the Pennsylvania Salt Manufacturing Company turned it into an industrial hub from 1852 to 1950.
The Burtner House, built in 1821, is Natrona Heights’ oldest building and now serves as a museum listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
Harrison Township, which contains Natrona Heights, was officially incorporated in March 1900 from parts of Fawn and East Deer Townships.
Located near the Allegheny River, Natrona Heights lies about 24 miles northeast of Pittsburgh within the Pittsburgh Metropolitan Statistical Area.
The Pennsalt Historic District features uniform brick rowhouses built between 1880 and 1920 that housed salt plant workers in Natrona Heights.
Natrona Heights is home to the 160‑year‑old Pittsburgh‑Tarentum Campmeeting Association, a Methodist camp, and the Pittsburgh Buddhist Center.
